alignments.note: Postpositive δέ realized by the verse-initial *but*.
Article surfaces as *the* under rule 19; split from its noun under rule 26.
Noun stands alone, its determiner having gone to the article.

δύναται is itself the modal lexeme, so *can* is its own word and not an auxiliary borrowed from the infinitive; the infinitive keeps *tame*. Rule 39's `οὐ δύναται` → *cannot* is not in question, the ASV writing the negation as a separate *no*.
οὐδείς takes *no*. Rules 41 and 59 are not in question: no separate negator stands in the clause for the indefinite to empty.

Partitive genitive ἀνθρώπων rendered by the singular *man* of *no man*. Rule 2 splits it from οὐδείς, both pieces remaining independently recoverable; the competing reading takes *no man* as one unit on οὐδείς with ἀνθρώπων unrepresented, but the ASV's *man* answers to this lexeme and nothing else. Rule 69's `οὐδένα` → *any man* is not the model, the *man* there being a supplied completion with no source token behind it.
Infinitive complement rendered by the bare *tame*, the modal riding with δύναται.

Verbless clause with no expressed subject, so under rule 68 the predicate carries both the supplied subject *it* and the copula *is*; κακόν is the substantival adjective serving as the nominal word of the predicate phrase, so under rule 58's substantival clause it also takes the supplied determiner *a*, ἀκατάστατον being only an attributive modifier inside the phrase. Discontinuous under rule 15.
Attributive adjective inside the predicate noun phrase keeps a bare *restless*; the determiner belongs to the nominal word under rule 58, not to the adjective it stands next to.
Second verbless clause, again with no expressed subject: the adjectival predicate takes the supplied *it is* along with its own *full* under rules 53 and 68.

Genitive complement rendered *of poison*; the ASV supplies no determiner, so under rule 21's determinerless clause the case preposition stays with the noun. Discontinuous around *deadly* under rule 15.
Attributive adjective takes the bare *deadly*, split from its noun under rule 26.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged. All 12 source and all 18 target ids partition exactly once; every unit is `aligned` with nonempty arrays and heads inside them, so rules 1, 3 and 10 hold.

Both verbless clauses lack an expressed subject, so rule 68 puts the supplied *it is* on the predicate rather than on any subject token; rules 53 and 63 do not reach them, there being no subject pronoun and no subject noun.

The *a* of *a restless evil* was re-checked. κακόν is a substantival A-NSN doing the nominal work, ἀκατάστατον only attributive, so the determiner is the nominal word's under rule 58 either way — by its main clause if κακόν is read as the phrase's noun, by its substantival clause (`νεκρῶν` → *the dead*) if it is read as an adjective. Rule 102 is not in question, the Greek being anarthrous with no article to take the determiner.
The one materially contested unit is the *no man* split across οὐδείς and ἀνθρώπων; the competing whole-phrase reading on οὐδείς with ἀνθρώπων unrepresented is named in the s007 note.

Both variant units are informational only: v008 (s005–s007) is underdetermined with the base among the compatible readings, and v009 (s008) is a selected base. Neither is marked FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE, so rule 97 is not engaged and no token needs `added`.
